title: What is tasawwuf?
summary: Tasawwuf as Hazrat Azam Pasha R.A. explains it while reading Nizam-ul-Amal-e-Fuqara: an inner knowledge whose source is the Qur'an and the Hadith, for the reform of both body and soul.

blocks.p: When Hazrat Azam Pasha R.A. began the dars of the book Nizam-ul-Amal-e-Fuqara, he explained what this knowledge is and what it is for. This article gathers what he says, in his own words where we can.
Hazrat calls it ilm-e-tasawwuf, or ilm-e-ladunni: a knowledge of the deen that is not seen from outside, but is found inwardly. He says more than once that it does not come from anywhere new.

blocks.q: The source of Sufism, or the knowledge of ladunni, is the Hadith and the Qur'an.

blocks.note: This passage is taken from the machine transcript of the recording, which is rough in places. The wording should be checked against the Urdu recording before approval. (Part 1, 53:28 to 55:08.)

blocks.p: Reading from the book, Hazrat teaches that a human being is the union of the soul and the body, and that each is reformed in its own way: the body by Shariat and Tariqat, the soul by Haqiqat and Marifat.

blocks.q: Shariat is to pray, to fast, to perform Hajj, to pay Zakat. All of this is Shariat. And what is Tariqat? To build a connection with Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.

blocks.p: For the soul, he says, Haqiqat means the hidden, inner things: Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the last Prophet, the angels, the whole order of creation. We have not seen them with our eyes; we come to know them through the Qur'an and the Ahadith.

blocks.q: The things of the soul cannot be seen; we come to know them through knowledge.

blocks.p: Why are there different ways, Qadri, Chishti, Naqshbandi and others? Hazrat answers: just as the jurists who draw from the Qur'an and Hadith differ (Hanafi, Shafi'i, Maliki, Hanbali), the Sufi ways are also ways of drawing from the Qur'an and Hadith. People's temperaments differ, and each looks for what suits him.

blocks.q: All the Sufi ways are good, good from head to toe. But along with that, in one the eyes are beautiful, in another the smile, in another the speech.

blocks.p: Hazrat explains the aim of the book this way: through this knowledge every person should live by the commands of Allah and of His Prophet ﷺ, choose the right path for guidance, take bai'at, repent, take up taqwa, and keep busy in worship.
